subject: Post-call: vendor parity & validation matrix for Meridian Health
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@meridianhealth.com>, Tom Blake <tom.blake@meridianhealth.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: vendor parity & validation matrix for Meridian Health

Hi Alicia / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so everyone is aligned.

Key pain points you reiterated:
- Inconsistent response latency when patients request record summaries (99th percentile spikes).
- Cost per inference is making scale for triage rules cost-prohibitive.
- Data isolation and auditability are required for compliance (SOC2 + regional retention).

Goals you shared:
1) Reduce 99th percentile latency for summaries to <500ms for short requests (<=256 tokens).
2) Bring per-session inference costs down ~30% relative to current provider to make feature economics viable.
3) Validate private deployment option for PHI-forwarding workflows.

Open items / asks we captured:
- Baseline throughput and latency numbers for 3 representative workloads (symptom triage, discharge summary, clinical note extraction).
- A short vendor parity matrix comparing Redwood vs current vendor + two finalists across latency, cost, security controls, and fallback options.
- A joint technical validation plan (3 tests) we can run in your sandbox next week.

Proposed next steps (please confirm):
1) I’ll share a filled parity matrix template and our suggested test cases by EOD Monday (attached).
2) Camila will follow up with a lightweight validation runbook and attachment with the test harness we’d like to use.
3) You’ll loop in procurement contacts if we move to a pilot/PoC and share any procurement constraints we should be aware of.

Attachments: 20270321_meridian_postcall_notes.pdf (post-call notes), vendor_parity_matrix_template.xlsx (matrix template).

If that aligns, can we lock a 60-minute sandbox kickoff for next Tuesday (Mar 23) 10:00–11:00 PT?

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@meridianhealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Tom Blake <tom.blake@meridianhealth.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: vendor parity & validation matrix for Meridian Health

Jonas — thanks for the thorough recap. This is helpful. Confirming a few details from our side: 

- Latency target: 500ms 99th sounds right for short summaries. For longer notes we accept higher but want predictable degradation.
- Cost target: 25–35% reduction is acceptable as a target band; procurement will want modeled TCO for 6/12/24 months.
- Privacy: our compliance team requires KMS-backed keys + quarterly audit logs where possible.

Open items we’ll provide this week:
- Example payloads (anonymized) for the three workloads — I’ll drop them in the Drive folder.
- Procurement constraints: we prefer a single monthly invoice and a 45-day net payment term for pilots.

Sandbox kickoff: Mar 23 at 10:00 PT works for us — reserving the hour.

Two small asks for your test plan: please include a test that demonstrates graceful fallback (model variant or region) if a node pool is overloaded, and one that captures token-level cost breakdowns per request.

Appreciate it —
Alicia Gomez
Director, Digital Patient Experience
Meridian Health
alicia.gomez@meridianhealth.com | (617) 555-2121

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@meridianhealth.com>, Tom Blake <tom.blake@meridianhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 07:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: vendor parity & validation matrix for Meridian Health

Camila / Marissa — forwarding Alicia’s notes. Key asks to bake into the validation plan: 

1) Test A — Latency profile: 1k request burst typical distribution, measure p50/p95/p99 across 256/1024 token batches. Accept criteria: p99 <= 500ms for 256 token payloads.
2) Test B — Cost modelling: run a 24-hour synthetic workload and produce per-request token cost & aggregation for projected monthly volume.
3) Test C — Resilience/fallback: simulate node pool eviction and verify automatic routing to fallbacks + no data leakage.

I’ve tentatively mapped responsibilities: Camila owns test harness + runbook, Marissa to own procurement pricing modeling and one-pager to present to procurement.

Also please add a short competitive note comparing Redwood’s approach to parametric competitors: we should highlight our prefix caching (saves tokens for repeat prompts), KV cache eviction semantics, and private deployment with KMS integration. Keep it two slides.

Thanks —
Jonas

Thanks — I prepared a concise validation runbook and a vendor parity slide (attached). Highlights: 

- Test harness: simple k6 + python harness that replays anonymized payloads at configurable concurrency; will produce p50/p95/p99 and token counts per request.
- Fallback test: harness triggers simulated node eviction and measures routing latency and success rate (we capture routing events in logs).
- Data isolation checklist: KMS key rotation steps, audit log export, and retention policy notes.

Attached: vendor_parity_matrix_filled.xlsx (sample comparison populated with Redwood vs CurrentVendor vs AltVendor) and validation_runbook.md (run steps).

Ask: Jonas — can you review the vendor parity slide for the two-slide summary to procurement? I’ll push the technical artifacts into the shared Drive folder tonight.

Cheers —
Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com

- Procurement confirmed 45-day net term for pilots is doable; they asked for a one-page pilot SOW template we can edit. I’ll bring that into the Drive.
- Compliance asked that the KMS integration diagram include who holds control (we will hold the keys for PHI flows). Could you add that to the parity slide?

Next steps we’ve agreed internally:
- Mar 26: procurement will send back a redlined pilot SOW draft.
- Mar 29: technical kickoff (hands-on with your harness) — Camila to run tests, Marissa to present cost model.
- Week of Apr 5: follow-up readout with results and recommendation.

Appreciate the quick turnaround. See you Tuesday for the harness run.

Best —
Alicia
